sanskrit: yo na yāti prasaṃkhyānam aspaṣṭo bhūmivardhanaḥ ayātayitvā vairāṇi so 'vasīdati gaur iva
english: He who does not undertake a reckoning, who is indistinct though a lord of the earth — he who does not pursue vengeance against enemies sinks down like a cow (mired in mud).

sanskrit: yo na yātayate vairam alpasattvodyamaḥ pumān aphalaṃ tasya janmāhaṃ manye durjātajāyinaḥ
english: The man of feeble courage and effort who does not requite enmity — I consider his birth fruitless, born as one born ill.

sanskrit: hairaṇyau bhavato bāhū śrutir bhavati pārthiva hatvā dviṣantaṃ saṃgrāme bhuktvā bāhvarjitaṃ vasu
english: Your arms are as golden, O king, and renown is gained by slaying the enemy in battle and then enjoying the wealth won by those arms.

sanskrit: hatvā cet puruṣo rājan nikartāram ariṃdama ahnāya narakaṃ gacchet svargeṇāsya sa saṃmitaḥ
english: If a man, O king, O tamer of foes, were to go to hell in an instant for slaying the one who wronged him, that hell would be equal to heaven for him.

sanskrit: amarṣajo hi saṃtāpaḥ pāvakād dīptimattaraḥ yenāham abhisaṃtapto na naktaṃ na divā śaye
english: For the burning anguish born of indignation is more blazing than fire; scorched by it, I sleep neither by night nor by day.

sanskrit: ayaṃ ca pārtho bībhatsur variṣṭho jyāvikarṣaṇe āste paramasaṃtapto nūnaṃ siṃha ivāśaye
english: And this Arjuna, son of Pṛthā — Bībhatsu, supreme in drawing the bowstring — sits utterly tormented, like a lion confined to a den.

sanskrit: yo 'yam eko 'bhimanute sarvāṃl loke dhanurbhṛtaḥ so 'yam ātmajam ūṣmāṇaṃ mahāhastīva yacchati
english: He who alone surpasses all bowmen in the world — this very man holds back his inner heat and ardour like a great elephant restrained.

sanskrit: nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca vṛddhā mātā ca vīrasūḥ tavaiva priyam icchanta āsate jaḍamūkavat
english: Nakula and Sahadeva, and our aged mother who bore heroes — wishing only for what pleases you, they sit as if dumb and mute.

sanskrit: sarve te priyam icchanti bāndhavāḥ saha sṛñjayaiḥ aham eko 'bhisaṃtapto mātā ca prativindhyataḥ
english: All your kinsmen along with the Sṛñjayas wish only what is dear to you; I alone am utterly scorched, as is the mother of Prativindhya.

sanskrit: priyam eva tu sarveṣāṃ yad bravīmy uta kiṃ cana sarve hī vyasanaṃ prāptāḥ sarve yuddhābhinandinaḥ
english: Whatever I say is indeed for the good of all; all have fallen into calamity, and all are eager for war.

sanskrit: netaḥ pāpīyasī kā cid āpad rājan bhaviṣyati yan no nīcair alpabalai rājyam ācchidya bhujyate
english: There can be no more wretched calamity than this, O king — that our kingdom is seized by base men of little strength and is being enjoyed by them.

sanskrit: śīladoṣād ghṛṇāviṣṭa ānṛśaṃsyāt paraṃtapa kleśāṃs titikṣase rājan nānyaḥ kaś cit praśaṃsati
english: Seized by pity through a flaw of character, out of tenderness, O scorcher of foes, you endure these sufferings, O king — no one else praises this.

sanskrit: ghṛṇī brāhmaṇarūpo 'si kathaṃ kṣatre ajāyathāḥ asyāṃ hi yonau jāyante prāyaśaḥ krūrabuddhayaḥ
english: You are compassionate and have the nature of a brahmin — how were you born into the kshatriya class? For in this womb they are mostly born with fierce minds.

sanskrit: aśrauṣīs tvaṃ rājadharmān yathā vai manur abravīt krūrān nikṛtisaṃyuktān vihitān aśamātmakān
english: You heard the duties of kings as Manu proclaimed them — cruel, combined with deceit, prescribed, and devoid of peace.

sanskrit: kartavye puruṣavyāghra kim āsse pīṭhasarpavat buddhyā vīryeṇa saṃyuktaḥ śrutenābhijanena ca
english: When action is called for, O tiger among men, why do you sit like a snake on a bench, though endowed with intellect, valour, learning, and noble birth?

sanskrit: tṛṇānāṃ muṣṭinaikena himavantaṃ tu parvatam channam icchasi kaunteya yo 'smān saṃvartum icchasi
english: With a single handful of grass you wish to cover the Himālaya mountain — such is what you wish when you want to conceal us, O son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: ajñātacaryā gūḍhena pṛthivyāṃ viśrutena ca divīva pārtha sūryeṇa na śakyā carituṃ tvayā
english: A life of passing unrecognised, in disguise, for one so widely known on earth — it cannot be done by you, O Pārtha, any more than the sun can move hidden in the sky.

sanskrit: bṛhacchāla ivānūpe śākhāpuṣpapalāśavān hastī śveta ivājñātaḥ kathaṃ jiṣṇuś cariṣyati
english: Like a great śāla tree in a marsh laden with branches, flowers, and leaves, like a white elephant — how can Jiṣṇu (Arjuna) pass about unknown?

sanskrit: imau ca siṃhasaṃkāśau bhrātarau sahitau śiśū nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca kathaṃ pārtha cariṣyataḥ
english: And these two brothers who resemble lions, these young men who go together — Nakula and Sahadeva — how will they wander about unrecognised, O Pārtha?

sanskrit: puṇyakīrtī rājaputrī draupadī vīrasūr iyam viśrutā katham ajñātā kṛṣṇā pārtha cariṣyati
english: Draupadī, the princess of sacred fame, the mother of heroes, widely renowned — how will Kṛṣṇā (Draupadī) wander unrecognised, O Pārtha?

sanskrit: māṃ cāpi rājañ jānanti ākumāram imāḥ prajāḥ ajñātacaryāṃ paśyāmi meror iva nigūhanam
english: And the people have known me since boyhood, O king; I see a life of concealment as impossible as hiding Mount Meru.

sanskrit: tathaiva bahavo 'smābhī rāṣṭrebhyo vipravāsitāḥ rājāno rājaputrāś ca dhṛtarāṣṭram anuvratāḥ
english: Likewise, many kings and princes devoted to Dhṛtarāṣṭra have been driven out of their kingdoms by us.

sanskrit: na hi te 'py upaśāmyanti nikṛtānāṃ nirākṛtāḥ avaśyaṃ tair nikartavyam asmākaṃ tatpriyaiṣibhiḥ
english: Those who have been wronged and expelled will not be pacified; they and those who seek their favour must inevitably do harm to us.

sanskrit: te 'py asmāsu prayuñjīran pracchannān subahūñ janān ācakṣīraṃś ca no jñātvā tan naḥ syāt sumahad bhayam
english: They too would deploy many spies against us in secret, and having identified us, would report us — that would be a very great danger for us.

sanskrit: asmābhir uṣitāḥ samyag vane māsās trayodaśa parimāṇena tān paśya tāvataḥ parivatsarān
english: We have duly dwelt in the forest for thirteen months by measure — reckon those as equivalent to that many full years.

sanskrit: asti māsaḥ pratinidhir yathā prāhur manīṣiṇaḥ pūtikān iva somasya tathedaṃ kriyatām iti
english: There is a substitute month, as the wise declare — just as pūtika plants (are used) in place of soma; let it be done accordingly.

sanskrit: atha vānaḍuhe rājan sādhave sādhuvāhine sauhityadānād ekasmād enasaḥ pratimucyate
english: Or again, O king, one is released from sin by a single act of gratifying feeding of an honest ox that carries a good burden.

sanskrit: tasmāc chatruvadhe rājan kriyatāṃ niścayas tvayā kṣatriyasya tu sarvasya nānyo dharmo 'sti saṃyugāt
english: Therefore, O king, let your resolve be fixed on the slaying of enemies; for a kshatriya there is no other duty than battle.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca bhīmasenavacaḥ śrutvā kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ niḥśvasya puruṣavyāghraḥ saṃpradadhyau paraṃtapaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard the words of Bhīmasena, Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī, that tiger among men and scorcher of foes, sighed deeply and fell into thought.

sanskrit: sa muhūrtam iva dhyātvā viniścityetikṛtyatām bhīmasenam idaṃ vākyam apadāntaram abravīt
english: Having reflected for a moment and determined what was to be done, he spoke these words to Bhīmasena without pause between syllables.

sanskrit: evam etan mahābāho yathā vadasi bhārata idam anyat samādhatsva vākyaṃ me vākyakovida
english: So it is, O mighty-armed one — as you say, O descendant of Bharata; but attend to this other matter of mine too, O one skilled in speech.

sanskrit: mahāpāpāni karmāṇi yāni kevalasāhasāt ārabhyante bhīmasena vyathante tāni bhārata
english: Those greatly sinful deeds that are undertaken through mere recklessness, O Bhīmasena, O descendant of Bharata — they come to grief.

sanskrit: sumantrite suvikrānte sukṛte suvicārite sidhyanty arthā mahābāho daivaṃ cātra pradakṣiṇam
english: Purposes succeed when well-counselled, well-executed, well-done, and well-considered, O mighty-armed one; and when they are thus, fate too becomes favourable.

sanskrit: tvaṃ tu kevalacāpalyād baladarpocchritaḥ svayam ārabdhavyam idaṃ karma manyase śṛṇu tatra me
english: But you, puffed up by pride in your strength, out of sheer impulsiveness, think this action should be undertaken by yourself alone — hear my view on that.

sanskrit: bhūriśravāḥ śalaś caiva jalasaṃdhaś ca vīryavān bhīṣmo droṇaś ca karṇaś ca droṇaputraś ca vīryavān
english: Bhūriśravas, Śala, and the mighty Jalasandha, Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Karṇa, and the valiant son of Droṇa —

sanskrit: dhārtarāṣṭrā durādharṣā duryodhanapurogamāḥ sarva eva kṛtāstrāś ca satataṃ cātatāyinaḥ
english: — the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, difficult to assail, headed by Duryodhana, all of them trained in weapons and perpetually set on aggression —

sanskrit: rājānaḥ pārthivāś caiva ye 'smābhir upatāpitāḥ saṃśritāḥ kauravaṃ pakṣaṃ jātasnehāś ca sāṃpratam
english: — and the kings and rulers whom we previously afflicted, who have now taken the Kaurava side and have developed affection for it —

sanskrit: duryodhanahite yuktā na tathāsmāsu bhārata pūrṇakośā balopetāḥ prayatiṣyanti rakṣaṇe
english: — devoted to Duryodhana's welfare, not so devoted to ours, O descendant of Bharata — with full treasuries and endowed with strength, they will strive to protect him.

sanskrit: sarve kauravasainyasya saputrāmātyasainikāḥ saṃvibhaktā hi mātrābhir bhogair api ca sarvaśaḥ
english: All the army of the Kauravas, together with their sons, ministers, and soldiers, have been given shares proportionate to their rank and enjoyed pleasures in every way.

sanskrit: duryodhanena te vīrā mānitāś ca viśeṣataḥ prāṇāṃs tyakṣyanti saṃgrāme iti me niścitā matiḥ
english: Those heroes have been especially honoured by Duryodhana; they will lay down their lives in battle — this is my firm conviction.

sanskrit: samā yady api bhīṣmasya vṛttir asmāsu teṣu ca droṇasya ca mahābāho kṛpasya ca mahātmanaḥ
english: Even if the conduct of Bhīṣma and Droṇa and the great-souled Kṛpa were equal toward us and toward them, O mighty-armed one —

sanskrit: avaśyaṃ rājapiṇḍas tair nirveśya iti me matiḥ tasmāt tyakṣyanti saṃgrāme prāṇān api sudustyajān
english: — they must inevitably repay the royal salt (i.e., the king's benefaction), this is my view; therefore they will give up their lives in battle, even those lives so hard to relinquish.

sanskrit: sarve divyāstravidvāṃsaḥ sarve dharmaparāyaṇāḥ ajeyāś ceti me buddhir api devaiḥ savāsavaiḥ
english: All know the divine weapons; all are devoted to righteousness; they are unconquerable — this is my understanding — even by the gods with Indra at their head.

sanskrit: amarṣī nityasaṃhṛṣṭas tatra karṇo mahārathaḥ sarvāstravid anādhṛṣya abhedyakavacāvṛtaḥ
english: And there among them is Karṇa, the great warrior, always exultant and full of wrath, master of all weapons, irresistible, clad in impenetrable armour.

sanskrit: anirjitya raṇe sarvān etān puruṣasattamān aśakyo hy asahāyena hantuṃ duryodhanas tvayā
english: Without conquering all these foremost of men in battle, it is impossible for you to slay Duryodhana singlehanded, without allies.

sanskrit: na nidrām adhigacchāmi cintayāno vṛkodara ati sarvān dhanurgrāhān sūtaputrasya lāghavam
english: I cannot attain sleep, O Vṛkodara (Bhīma), when I reflect on the swiftness of the charioteer's son (Karṇa) which surpasses all bowmen.

sanskrit: etad vacanam ājñāya bhīmaseno 'tyamarṣaṇaḥ babhūva vimanās trasto na caivovāca kiṃ cana
english: Hearing this speech, Bhīmasena, extremely wrathful by nature, became disheartened and frightened, and said nothing at all.

sanskrit: tayoḥ saṃvadator evaṃ tadā pāṇḍavayor dvayoḥ ājagāma mahāyogī vyāsaḥ satyavatīsutaḥ
english: While those two Pāṇḍavas were thus conversing together, the great yogin Vyāsa, son of Satyavatī, arrived.

sanskrit: so 'bhigamya yathānyāyaṃ pāṇḍavaiḥ pratipūjitaḥ yudhiṣṭhiram idaṃ vākyam uvāca vadatāṃ varaḥ
english: Having approached and been duly honoured by the Pāṇḍavas, he spoke these words to Yudhiṣṭhira, that best of speakers.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira mahābāho vedmi te hṛdi mānasam manīṣayā tataḥ kṣipram āgato 'smi nararṣabha
english: O Yudhiṣṭhira, O mighty-armed one, I know what is in your heart and mind; it is because of this wisdom that I have come quickly, O bull among men.

sanskrit: bhīṣmād droṇāt kṛpāt karṇād droṇaputrāc ca bhārata yat te bhayam amitraghna hṛdi saṃparivartate
english: The fear of Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Kṛpa, Karṇa, and the son of Droṇa, O descendant of Bharata, O slayer of enemies — that which revolves in your heart —

sanskrit: tat te 'haṃ nāśayiṣyāmi vidhidṛṣṭena hetunā tac chrutvā dhṛtim āsthāya karmaṇā pratipādaya
english: — that I will destroy for you by a means prescribed by scriptural rule; having heard it, take courage and implement it through action.

sanskrit: tata ekāntam unnīya pārāśaryo yudhiṣṭhiram abravīd upapannārtham idaṃ vākyaviśāradaḥ
english: Then the son of Parāśara (Vyāsa), skilled in speech, led Yudhiṣṭhira aside in private and spoke to him these words full of pertinent meaning.

sanskrit: śreyasas te paraḥ kālaḥ prāpto bharatasattama yenābhibhavitā śatrūn raṇe pārtho dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: The supreme time of your welfare has arrived, O best of the Bharatas — the time when Arjuna, Dhanaṃjaya son of Pṛthā, will overcome the enemies in battle.

sanskrit: gṛhāṇemāṃ mayā proktāṃ siddhiṃ mūrtimatīm iva vidyāṃ pratismṛtiṃ nāma prapannāya bravīmi te yām avāpya mahābāhur arjunaḥ sādhayiṣyati
english: Receive this knowledge called Pratismṛti (the Recollection) which I now declare — it is as if success itself made incarnate; I speak it to you as a supplicant, and having obtained it, the mighty-armed Arjuna will accomplish his purpose.

sanskrit: astrahetor mahendraṃ ca rudraṃ caivābhigacchatu varuṇaṃ ca dhaneśaṃ ca dharmarājaṃ ca pāṇḍava śakto hy eṣa surān draṣṭuṃ tapasā vikrameṇa ca
english: For the sake of weapons let him approach Mahendra (Indra), Rudra, Varuṇa, the Lord of Wealth (Kubera), and the King of Dharma (Yama), O Pāṇḍava; for he is capable of seeing the gods through both austerity and valour.

sanskrit: ṛṣir eṣa mahātejā nārāyaṇasahāyavān purāṇaḥ śāśvato devo viṣṇor aṃśaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: This one (Arjuna) is a seer of great splendour, accompanied by Nārāyaṇa; he is ancient, eternal, divine — a portion of Viṣṇu, everlasting.

sanskrit: astrāṇīndrāc ca rudrāc ca lokapālebhya eva ca samādāya mahābāhur mahat karma kariṣyati
english: Having received the weapons from Indra, from Rudra, and from the guardians of the worlds, the mighty-armed one will accomplish a great deed.

sanskrit: vanād asmāc ca kaunteya vanam anyad vicintyatām nivāsārthāya yad yuktaṃ bhaved vaḥ pṛthivīpate
english: And from this forest, O son of Kuntī, let another forest be sought out — whatever would be fitting for your residence, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: ekatra ciravāso hi na prītijanano bhavet tāpasānāṃ ca śāntānāṃ bhaved udvegakārakaḥ
english: For a prolonged stay in one place would not be pleasing, and it would cause disturbance to the peaceful ascetics living there.

sanskrit: mṛgāṇām upayogaś ca vīrudoṣadhisaṃkṣayaḥ bibharṣi hi bahūn viprān vedavedāṅgapāragān
english: There would also be the consumption of game and the depletion of plants and herbs; and you are supporting many brahmin scholars versed in the Vedas and their branches.

sanskrit: evam uktvā prapannāya śucaye bhagavān prabhuḥ provāca yogatattvajño yogavidyām anuttamām
english: Having spoken thus, the blessed lord (Vyāsa), the knower of the truth of yoga, imparted to the pure supplicant the unsurpassed knowledge of yoga.

sanskrit: dharmarājñe tadā dhīmān vyāsaḥ satyavatīsutaḥ anujñāya ca kaunteyaṃ tatraivāntaradhīyata
english: The wise Vyāsa, son of Satyavatī, having imparted it to the King of Dharma and having taken leave of the son of Kuntī, vanished there and then.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiras tu dharmātmā tad brahma manasā yataḥ dhārayām āsa medhāvī kāle kāle samabhyasan
english: But Yudhiṣṭhira, righteous in soul, that wise one, restrained in mind, retained that sacred knowledge, practising it repeatedly from time to time.

sanskrit: sa vyāsavākyamudito vanād dvaitavanāt tataḥ yayau sarasvatītīre kāmyakaṃ nāma kānanam
english: Gladdened by Vyāsa's words, he then departed from Dvaitavana forest and went to the forest named Kāmyaka on the bank of the Sarasvatī.

sanskrit: tam anvayur mahārāja śikṣākṣaravidas tathā brāhmaṇās tapasā yuktā devendram ṛṣayo yathā
english: O great king, brahmin scholars versed in the syllables of learning, endowed with austerity, followed him, as the sages follow the lord of the gods.

sanskrit: tataḥ kāmyakam āsādya punas te bharatarṣabhāḥ nyaviśanta mahātmānaḥ sāmātyāḥ sapadānugāḥ
english: Having reached Kāmyaka, those bulls of the Bharata line, great-souled, along with their ministers and followers, settled there again.

sanskrit: tatra te nyavasan rājan kaṃ cit kālaṃ manasvinaḥ dhanurvedaparā vīrāḥ śṛṇvānā vedam uttamam
english: There they dwelt for some time, O king, those men of firm resolve, those heroes devoted to the science of archery, listening to the highest Veda.

sanskrit: caranto mṛgayāṃ nityaṃ śuddhair bāṇair mṛgārthinaḥ pitṛdaivataviprebhyo nirvapanto yathāvidhi
english: Ranging the forest in daily hunting, seeking game with pure arrows, they made oblations to the ancestors, the gods, and the brahmins according to injunction.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca kasya cit tv atha kālasya dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ saṃsmṛtya munisaṃdeśam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, after some time had passed, King Dharmarāja Yudhiṣṭhira, recalling the sage's instruction, spoke these words.

sanskrit: vivikte viditaprajñam arjunaṃ bharatarṣabham sāntvapūrvaṃ smitaṃ kṛtvā pāṇinā parisaṃspṛśan
english: In a secluded place, touching him with his hand, smiling gently, he addressed Arjuna, that bull of the Bharatas, whose wisdom is well-known.

sanskrit: sa muhūrtam iva dhyātvā vanavāsam ariṃdamaḥ dhanaṃjayaṃ dharmarājo rahasīdam uvāca ha
english: Having reflected for a moment on their forest exile, the dharma-king, tamer of foes, spoke these words to Dhanaṃjaya in private.

sanskrit: bhīṣme droṇe kṛpe karṇe droṇaputre ca bhārata dhanurvedaś catuṣpāda eteṣv adya pratiṣṭhitaḥ
english: In Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Kṛpa, Karṇa, and the son of Droṇa, O descendant of Bharata — in these five today is established the four-footed science of archery.

sanskrit: brāhmaṃ daivam āsuraṃ ca saprayogacikitsitam sarvāstrāṇāṃ prayogaṃ ca te 'bhijānanti kṛtsnaśaḥ
english: The Brahmā, divine, and demoniac (classes of weapons), along with their application and remedy, and the deployment of all weapons — they know all this in its entirety.

sanskrit: te sarve dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putreṇa parisāntvitāḥ saṃvibhaktāś ca tuṣṭāś ca guruvat teṣu vartate
english: All of them have been conciliated by the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, given their portions, and satisfied; he behaves toward them as if they were his gurus.

sanskrit: sarvayodheṣu caivāsya sadā vṛttir anuttamā śaktiṃ na hāpayiṣyanti te kāle pratipūjitāh
english: And his conduct toward all warriors is ever excellent; honoured at the proper time, they will not fail to exert their full strength.

sanskrit: adya ceyaṃ mahī kṛtsnā duryodhanavaśānugā tvayi vyapāśrayo 'smākaṃ tvayi bhāraḥ samāhitaḥ tatra kṛtyaṃ prapaśyāmi prāptakālam ariṃdama
english: Today this entire earth follows under Duryodhana's sway; on you our refuge rests, on you the burden is placed — in that regard I see a task that the present time calls for, O tamer of foes.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇadvaipāyanāt tāta gṛhītopaniṣan mayā tayā prayuktayā samyag jagat sarvaṃ prakāśate tena tvaṃ brahmaṇā tāta saṃyuktaḥ susamāhitaḥ
english: From Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana (Vyāsa) I have received the secret wisdom, dear one; through that knowledge properly employed the whole world is illuminated — with that sacred wisdom, dear one, be united, with mind fully composed.

sanskrit: devatānāṃ yathākālaṃ prasādaṃ pratipālaya tapasā yojayātmānam ugreṇa bharatarṣabha
english: Wait upon the grace of the gods at the proper time; yoke yourself to fierce austerity, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: dhanuṣmān kavacī khaḍgī muniḥ sārasamanvitaḥ na kasya cid dadan mārgaṃ gaccha tātottarāṃ diśam indre hy astrāṇi divyāni samastāni dhanaṃjaya
english: Bearing your bow, clad in armour, carrying your sword, sage-like and possessed of essence, yielding the path to none, go northward, dear one — for in Indra all the divine weapons in their entirety dwell, O Dhanaṃjaya.
